doc.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024

title: Mr. Oaks's humiliation that drove him to practice
summary: In the Riverside Polytechnic advanced band the director mocked his sound; Hal responded by practicing hours daily.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: good player, I was just in the ninth grade. So the high school in Riverside, there’s only one high school, Riverside Polytechnic High. And they had a great band and they had — there were three junior high schools that fed into the high school so they picked all three first chair junior high players to put in the advanced band. So I was next to last chair. And they were supposed to have a concert the next day at an elementary school, you know, a big thing for us. And so the trumpet player, the first trumpet player, had a solo. And while we were rehearsing the tune he messed up the trumpet solo right from the beginning. So Mr. Oaks, our band director, slammed down the baton, looked over his glasses at him and said, “Okay let’s start from Letter C” (the trumpet solo). He wasn’t prepared for that and then he screwed it up worse. And then a third time, just as bad. So he went to the second player. He wasn’t prepared. He missed it. And so he went right down the row of trumpets. When it got to me I was shaking. When I started playing he threw down the baton and said, “What are you doing even playing the trumpet? You sound like a billy goat.” And he embarrassed me so much that if there would have been a hole I would have crawled in to it. He was the one that motivated me to start practicing. Because when I went home I started practicing between three to five hours and then pretty soon it was four to six hours every day after school because I was going to show him I could play the trumpet. So that’s where I started.
I love that because there’s two spots in that story where I thought it was going somewhere and it didn’t. I thought you know it finally got to you and you played it beautifully.
Yes. But then the fact that he embarrassed you and instead of quitting you went the other direction.
